ideas.title: Other: Send only the route's i18n namespaces to the client
ideas.description:
i18n/request.ts loads all 22 namespaces (568 KB of JSON in es) and app/[locale]/layout.tsx:75,95 passes them whole to NextIntlClientProvider. Every HTML document weighs 160-200 KB gzip, and about 158 KB gzip of that is messages, on public pages too (/@handle, booking, help center). Measured in docs/benchmark/performance.md (4x CPU, 4G). First scope: the root layout picks only 'common', each app layout adds a nested provider with its own namespace, and public pages add theirs. Server components keep reading everything through getTranslations. Expected: -130 to 150 KB gzip per document, and less on every router.refresh.

Priority: high. Effort: M.

ideas.title: Other: Dedupe the session per request with React cache() and parallelize layout reads
ideas.description:
getCurrentUser (lib/session.ts:54-71) runs 3 times per request: in Header, in the app layout and in the page. Each call does getServerSession, getUserByEmail and resolveWorkspace (up to 4 queries), and in DEMO_MODE it also writes UPDATE users SET seeded_at. The app layout adds countDueTasks and about 12 sequential getTranslations calls. Locally TTFB is 20-40 ms, but on Turso every query is a round-trip. First scope: wrap getCurrentUser in cache(), use Promise.all in app/[locale]/app/layout.tsx, and keep the seeded flag in memory for the demo user.

Priority: high. Effort: S.

ideas.title: Other: Split app CSS per app instead of importing every app's stylesheet in the shell
ideas.description:
app/[locale]/app/layout.tsx:12-27 imports the CSS of all 11 apps plus @xyflow/react/dist/style.css, and the root layout adds board-public.css to every page. Every app page loads 15 render-blocking stylesheets (96 KB gzip, measured). First scope: move each import to app/[locale]/app/<app>/layout.tsx, keep only app.css and color.css in the shell, and load the xyflow CSS only in the Flow editor.

Priority: high. Effort: S.

ideas.title: Docs: Server-render block content so the editor does not shift on load
ideas.description:
DocsBlockEditor.tsx:97-107 writes el.innerHTML = block.content in a useLayoutEffect, so the server HTML has empty contentEditable blocks and the text only appears after hydration. Measured on a 60-block page with 4x CPU and 4G: LCP 1.85 s (other pages are around 0.9 s) and CLS 0.215. Five blocks grow from 34 to 90 px at about 2 s. The Docs tree that is portaled into #side-branch adds 0.048 more. Notion opens pages with their text already painted. First scope: render the first pass with dangerouslySetInnerHTML (keeping the anti-clobber effect for later changes) and reserve the height of #side-branch.

Priority: high. Effort: S.

ideas.title: Notes: Use server data as initial state and stop loading 500 full notes
ideas.description:
Notes scores CLS 0.133 (measured, 4x CPU): NotesApp.tsx:178,201 refetches /api/notes on mount and the main panel re-lays out. listNotes (lib/notes.ts:282-284) does SELECT n.* (full blocks and body_text) for up to 500 rows to show a snippet, and the list is not virtualized. It shares the Docs editor, so it also inherits the empty-blocks-on-SSR issue. First scope: initialize state from the server component, select only the needed columns plus substr(body_text,1,200), and paginate or virtualize the list.

Priority: medium. Effort: M.

ideas.title: Other: Avoid the full router.refresh() when the timezone cookie is first set
ideas.description:
On the first visit to the app, components/app/TimezoneCookie.tsx:46 sets the tz cookie and calls router.refresh(). That refetches the whole RSC tree (about 159 KB, mostly i18n messages) and costs one extra server render. Measured: 724 KB total on a first visit versus 561 KB on a returning visit, with the same FCP and LCP. First scope: refresh only on pages whose dates depend on 'today', or render those dates on the client. Once i18n messages are trimmed per route, the refresh gets cheaper by itself.

Priority: medium. Effort: S.

ideas.title: Board: Make Excalidraw onChange cheap and preload the editor from the list
ideas.description:
Opening a board downloads 587 KB of gzip JS from the lazy Excalidraw chunks. BoardEditor.tsx:403-422 computes signature() over every element and calls setState('dirty') on every Excalidraw change, including appState-only changes such as picking a tool. Pressing 'r' measured an INP of 136-320 ms at 4x CPU, the only page over 200 ms. The page also calls getBoard twice (generateMetadata and the page). First scope: skip appState-only changes, use getSceneVersion for the signature, skip setState when already dirty, import() ExcalidrawCanvas on hover in BoardList, and wrap getBoard in cache().

Priority: medium. Effort: M.

ideas.title: Chat: Replace 3-second full polling with incremental fetches
ideas.description:
ConversationClient.tsx:280-291 polls the full message list, typing status and the conversation every 3 s (about 60 requests per minute per open tab). InboxShell.tsx:139-171 polls conversations every 10 s. listChatConversations (lib/chat-data.ts:911-928) runs 2-3 correlated subqueries per row. On Turso, every open tab is constant load. Intercom pushes updates over a socket. First scope: add ?since=<updated_at> so only new messages are fetched, pause polling while document.hidden, and denormalize last_message_body onto chat_conversations.

Priority: medium. Effort: M.

ideas.title: Agents: Index the 7-day stats queries and stop loading them in the Flow editor
ideas.description:
listAgents (lib/agents.ts:157-176) aggregates agent_conversations with WHERE user_id AND created_at and agent_feedback with WHERE user_id, but both tables only have agent_id indexes. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows a SCAN of each table, so the cost grows with every conversation. The Flow editor page (app/[locale]/app/flow/[id]/page.tsx:27-30) loads the full listAgents, stats included, just for a picker. First scope: a migration adding agent_conversations(user_id, created_at) and agent_feedback(user_id, agent_id), plus a light listAgentOptions for the pickers.

Priority: medium. Effort: S.

ideas.title: Link: Daily click rollups for analytics and record clicks after the redirect
ideas.description:
/api/links/analytics takes 23 ms with only 6,000 clicks, 5 times slower than any other list endpoint (measured). The plan joins links and clicks and builds a temp B-tree for GROUP BY, so it grows linearly with clicks. recordClick (lib/track.ts:145) also writes synchronously before the 302, which on Turso adds a round-trip to every redirect. Dub keeps clicks in a separate events store. First scope: a link_clicks_daily(link_id, day, country, device, referrer, count) table updated in the same batch, analytics reading from it, and the clicks INSERT moved into after().

Priority: medium. Effort: M.

ideas.title: Docs: Return summaries from GET /api/docs/pages and paginate
ideas.description:
GET /api/docs/pages uses listDocPages (lib/docs.ts:250-256), which returns SELECT * with every page's content and no limit: 375 KB for 31 pages (measured). The lean listDocPageSummaries (lib/docs.ts:263) already exists. First scope: use the summaries in the list endpoint, add limit and cursor parameters, and keep content on GET /api/docs/pages/:id.

Priority: low. Effort: S.

ideas.title: Other: Run PRAGMA optimize and add indexes for the remaining sort orders
ideas.description:
The database has no sqlite_stat1, so the planner picks odd indexes: sorting contacts by name uses idx_crm_contacts_score, and the link count uses idx_links_user_creator. Several sorts build a temp B-tree: contacts by name and email with COLLATE NOCASE (lib/crm.ts:575-578), links by clicks (lib/links.ts:204), and Docs by position. That is cheap today and will not be at 50k rows. First scope: run PRAGMA optimize from the hourly cron, and add indexes on (user_id, first_name COLLATE NOCASE, last_name COLLATE NOCASE) and (user_id, clicks DESC).

Priority: low. Effort: S.
